A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with DLHP renamed S2P2 and the title changed. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on eight real-world datasets, synthetic Poisson and multivariate Hawkes processes, runtime measurements, ablations, and calibration analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds synthetic self-correcting, univariate Hawkes, and long-range dependency experiments, alongside expanded baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The LLH recurrence, input-dependent dynamics, discretization, stacked architecture, likelihood objective, and parallel-scan algorithms remain unchanged despite renaming. A limited removal is v1's optional trained linear-probe head for next-event-time prediction (Appendix D.1, Table 9); v2 reports intensity-based expected-time prediction without that auxiliary variant.

E1.justification: The eight real-world datasets and existing Poisson and multivariate Hawkes coverage remain. v2 substantially broadens synthetic coverage with self-correcting dynamics and a controlled trigger–target process containing long delays and distractor events, testing conditions absent from v1 (Section 5, Appendices D.4–D.5).

E2.justification: Mamba Hawkes Process (MHP), discussed but not evaluated in v1, becomes an evaluated comparator across the real-world benchmarks, calibration analyses, and retained synthetic experiments. Adding this closely related SSM-based competitor materially strengthens the comparison; the original six baselines remain.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 replaces thinning-based next-time estimation with trapezoidal integration. The reported MIMIC-II architecture changes from h=256, p=64, L=2 to h=64, p=16, L=2. v2 also introduces composite ranking and new synthetic protocols while retaining real-world splits. The new self-correcting coefficient is inconsistent between Section 5 and Appendix D.4.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled intensity-recovery analyses for self-correcting and univariate Hawkes processes, plus qualitative and quantitative tests of long-range dependency recovery (Appendices D.4–D.5). These directly probe expressivity and memory. The original forward/backward ZOH and input-dependence ablation is retained unchanged, and the speed study moves to Appendix B.5.

E5.justification: v2 extends mean-and-standard-deviation reporting to next-event RMSE, mark accuracy, and calibration results (Tables 2 and 15), whereas their v1 counterparts reported point values. Five-seed likelihood reporting and 20-seed runtime summaries already existed. This broadens uncertainty disclosure without establishing an increase in training runs or introducing significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds MHP results and new synthetic findings, including long-range likelihood ratios of 97.8% for S2P2, 99.7% for AttNHP, and 87.9% for NHP (Table 13). Accuracy, RMSE, and calibration entries are extensively revised. MIMIC-II likelihood changes from 1.243 to 0.919 under a smaller architecture, and the aggregate likelihood advantage changes from 38% to 33%. Revised RMSE values use a different estimator, precluding simple same-setting performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 changes the stated LHP positivity restriction from nonnegative beta to nonnegative exp(-beta), alongside nonnegative alpha. Appendix B.5 extends the theoretical complexity analysis to MHP. The principal LLH and ZOH derivations remain, and no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains an expressive continuous-time MTPP combining LLH layers with efficient parallel computation. v2 revises the headline likelihood advantage from 38% to 33% and adds an explicit claim of best-or-second-best average performance across six metrics, supported by a new composite ranking.

C2.justification: Sections 7–8 substantially expand applicability and mechanism discussion. Beyond v1's implementation-complexity and interpretability caveats, v2 discusses numerical integration for expected times, inability to represent temporal point masses, unsuitability when interpretation is crucial, and untested censored/adversarial conditions. It also expands the continuous-state explanation and changes the multivariate Hawkes interpretation to emphasize comparable performance across methods.

D1.justification: v1 promises a release and mentions supplementary code; v2 reports completed EasyTPP integration, provides integration and reproduction-repository links, and offers checkpoints on request. It documents EHRSHOT preparation code and credentialed-access restrictions, dates baseline implementations to May 2025, and supplies MHP search settings and architectures for the new synthetic studies.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on mixed-type events, SSM approximation and interpretability, and censored/adversarial point processes, while removing some earlier references such as the CNN-based discussion. MHP was already cited, but its relationship is sharpened around discrete encoder–decoder states versus continuously evolving states. The underlying Hawkes/SSM research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and method exposition, changes the title and model terminology, and reorders the method subsections. Synthetic and real-world experiments become separate sections, a dedicated discussion is added, and runtime material moves to the appendix. These changes go well beyond accommodating additional experiments.

P2.justification: The original three-part architecture figure is split and redrawn into v2 Figures 1a and 2, with a new ranking summary in Figure 1b. Appendix accuracy and RMSE tables are incorporated into the main three-part Table 2. New synthetic plots are added, multivariate Hawkes panels are consolidated, and the runtime figure moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves important evidential gaps by evaluating the closely related MHP baseline and directly testing long-range dependency recovery, rather than relying mainly on scaling evidence. Expanded uncertainty reporting, clearer exposition, and concrete reproduction/access information further improve assessability. These gains outweigh localized inconsistencies: the self-correcting formula differs between Section 5 and Appendix D.4, and some IFTPP/MHP ranks in Figure 1b disagree with Table 2. The improvement rests on stronger validation and transparency, not higher reported performance.
